paragraphs: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Matya. (A tanna mentioned in the Mishnah.)

In Eduyot, three matters were brought before Rabbi Yishmael. He gave no ruling of either prohibition or permission, and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Matya explained them. Yuḥasin says that he lived at the time Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya was appointed. But this provides little proof, since Eduyot mentions tannaim from the preceding generation as well as from later generations.[^1]

notes.text: Hyman cites Eduyot, chapter 2, mishnah 2 (פ״ב מ״ב). That locator is retained here as his citation; it has not been checked against a named edition or converted to different modern numbering. Yuḥasin is the title as cited, without an edition identification. The familiar initials ראב״ע are rendered Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya in the context of the appointment; Hyman’s objection to the chronological inference is preserved.
